title: fix(knowledge-pgvector): dropSource removes a source another process is building, and that build cannot bring it back
body:
Fixes #37732

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：使用 pgvector 知识库的多节点部署里，删除一个知识源时如果另一个节点正在重建它，以前会留下一代残余索引，或者被那次重建悄悄"复活"；现在删干净，那次重建会被拒绝并停下。单节点和 turso 存储没有变化。
- 为什么做：这是 AI 知识库"索引分代与重建"专项的收尾，替多节点自托管部署补上删源时的并发漏洞，并第一次在真实的 PostgreSQL 上跑了这组用例。
- 出错会怎样：最坏的情况是一次正在进行的重建被拒绝，需要再重建一次；改动只在 pgvector 存储里，可以直接撤回。
- 要你做什么：无。

## What changes

`IKnowledgeAdapter.dropSource` (packages/spec/src/contracts/knowledge-adapter.ts) drops "every generation, the one under construction included". The live cells this PR adds measured two places where the pgvector store did not hold to that while another process was building the same source and held its builder lock. The contract sentence is right and stays as it is. The adapter is fixed.

1. **The drop missed a generation that a waiting transaction opened.** `beginBuild` opens its generation in a transaction that row-locks the source's generations (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE`). A drop that arrived during that transaction waited on the row lock. Under READ COMMITTED, the waiting statement then re-read only the rows it had already seen, so it never saw the new `building` row. It retired the active generation and left the new one `building`, where the other build kept writing and then completed it. Measured live before the fix: `heldFor` after the drop was `["2:fp-fence:b:building"]`. `dropSource` still takes the row lock first, which waits for that transaction. It then retires everything with one statement of its own (an `UPDATE` that sets `state = 'retired'` on every row of the source not already retired), and that statement sees the row the waited-on transaction committed.
2. **The other build's next write brought the dropped source back.** That process still held the advisory lock, so `fenceBuild` let the call through. `writeTarget` then found no generation and opened a new **active** one (the rule that a source holding nothing takes the first fingerprint it is handed). The page landed there, and so did the rest of the walk. Measured live before the fix: every case's `upsert` after the drop resolved, and the walk through `KnowledgeService` answered `ok: true`. Now a call of a build this adapter began (`ctx.reason === 'reindex'`) goes only to the generation that build began. When that generation is no longer `active` or `building`, the build ends: the entry in `builds` is dropped, the builder lock is let go, and the call is refused `LOCK_CONFLICT` (409). `completeBuild` makes the same check first. Before, a completion with no write since the drop threw a plain `Error` with no code.
3. `generationReplaced` is folded into `buildEnded`, which says "dropped or replaced" and has the same code and status (`LOCK_CONFLICT`, 409). No consumer parses its text.

**turso parity (read, not run).** turso has no builder lock and no per-build fence. Its `dropSource` is one write transaction, and SQLite serializes it against a concurrent `beginBuild` or `completeBuild` transaction, so case 1 has no turso counterpart. Case 2 does: a build in another process that keeps going after the drop writes into a fresh active generation (turso-adapter.ts `writeTarget`, which opens one for a source that holds nothing), so on turso a dropped source can come back the same way. This PR makes no turso change, as the card asks.

## Tests

Six live cells, in a new top-level `describe` of `build-fence.live-postgres.test.ts`, the existing build-fence harness file. Each cell uses two adapters on one schema, each with its own pool and its own builder locks, standing for two processes:

- a build beside the active generation, then a drop: nothing is held afterwards; the build's next page and its completion are refused `LOCK_CONFLICT`; `indexStatus` answers `{}`; the lock was let go, so the source builds again from nothing;
- a rebuild inside the active generation, then a drop: the same outcome;
- a build with no write since the drop is refused at its completion alone;
- a page whose embedding was under way when the drop committed is not written anywhere;
- a drop that waits on another process's `beginBuild` transaction, which is held at its `COMMIT` by a gated pool, retires the generation that transaction opened;
- through `KnowledgeService`: a walk whose source another process drops after page 1 stops (`ok: false`, one page), and nothing is left.

Local run, on a PostgreSQL 16.15 installed in the container with pgvector 0.6.0 (apt `postgresql-16-pgvector`; CI's image is pgvector 0.8.7-pg16):

<details><summary>Before the fix (the cells at a3c456e61d, adapter as on main)</summary>

```
× a build beside the active generation … — promise resolved "undefined" instead of rejecting
× a rebuild inside the active generation … — promise resolved "undefined" instead of rejecting
× a build's page whose embedding is under way … — promise resolved "undefined" instead of rejecting
× a drop that waits on another process's beginBuild transaction … — generations: ["2:fp-fence:b:building"]
× through KnowledgeService … — expected { ok: true, … } to match object { ok: false, indexed: 100 }
```
The first run of that cell was confounded: the dropping adapter's first-call DDL (`CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`) waited on the build's open transaction, so the drop's locking read ran after the commit and saw the row. The cell now makes the dropping process ready first and waits for the `FOR UPDATE` statement itself. The listed verdict comes from that corrected cell.
</details>

<details><summary>After the fix, the whole package (unit and live)</summary>

At 16e31bf1a8, with `OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` set and `OS_EXPECT_LIVE_DIALECT_MATRIX=1`:
```
pnpm --filter @objectstack/knowledge-pgvector exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2
 Test Files  9 passed (9)
      Tests  94 passed (94)
```
This is 74 live cells that were already there (none of them had run on any head before; on main at 0a3ea67c2c, unchanged, they pass 74/74 here), the 6 new live cells, and 14 unit tests. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/knowledge-pgvector build` and `typecheck` both exit 0; `check:test-typecheck` compiles the test layer with 0 errors. That run went outside the shared verify lock, which was held by a dogfood run for more than 25 minutes; the run is about 40 s at `--maxWorkers=2`.
</details>

<details><summary>Ablations (each one mutates the committed adapter, runs the six cells, then restores and checks that `git diff HEAD` is empty; the tests import `src`, so no dist is involved)</summary>

- Drop's retirement put back to the per-row loop over what the locking read returned: only the `beginBuild`-transaction cell goes red (1 failed, 5 passed).
- The build-generation guard in `writeTarget` disabled (`build` forced to `undefined`): 5 cells go red, and only the completion-alone cell passes.
- The new first check in `completeBuild` deleted: only the completion-alone cell goes red.
</details>

CI: these cells run in **Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)**, step "Run the pgvector knowledge store against live PostgreSQL". That job runs on a `merge_group` entry whose diff hits the `temporal_live` paths (this diff does: `packages/plugins/knowledge-pgvector/**`) and on main's full battery. It never runs on `pull_request`, and it is not in the required set, so its queue run is advisory. Test Core runs the package's unit files; there the live files are a named skip.

## Acceptance notes

- Boundary, not changed here: a drop of a source that holds **nothing**, racing a `beginBuild` that opens the source's first generation, has no row to wait on. It is settled as drop-then-build, and the build's generation is kept. A source the drop did not see had nothing to drop.
- Boundary, not changed here: event-sync writes (`reason` other than `reindex`) are not fenced. One that arrives after a drop opens a fresh active generation, as for any source that holds nothing. The service stops sending them once the source is unregistered in that process.
- Observed while measuring: a fresh adapter's first call runs the store's DDL, and `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` on the generation table waits behind any open write transaction on that table, even when the index exists. The wait is short and is not a defect. It is noted because it hid the race in the first run.
- turso parity: as stated above. Case 2's counterpart on turso is read, not run, and is not filed.

## Verification

Read first:
1. `packages/plugins/knowledge-pgvector/src/pgvector-adapter.ts`, the `build` branch at the top of `writeTarget`. This is the riskiest hunk: every walk call now goes through it, and a wrong match would refuse a healthy build.
2. `dropSource`: the row lock, then the one `UPDATE`.
3. The completion check that comes first in `completeBuild`.

Two-minute check, with `OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` pointing at a PostgreSQL that has pgvector: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/knowledge-pgvector exec vitest run build-fence.live-postgres -t "another process"`. Expected: 6 passed.
